SOFTWARE · FIELD NOTE 01

A quieter bot is a better bot

Useful automation should leave a little room for everyone else. A group-chat bot is no exception.

Fetch when there is a reason

A weather binding is a preference, not a reason to query every provider forever. The bot fetches a region when someone asks, when a greeting needs it, or when an explicitly configured notification is due. A short per-region cache serves nearby requests; a per-region lock prevents simultaneous requests from repeating the same work.

Keep slow work off the conversation path

Research, video metadata and image recognition can take longer than an ordinary message. Independent jobs, concurrency bounds and time budgets let those tasks finish without making unrelated groups wait. A model listing alone does not prove a model can answer: successful ordinary responses build a preference queue instead.

Collect less, preserve better

A picture is not necessarily a sticker. Explicit sticker metadata and actual GIF headers are stronger evidence than a word in a CDN URL. Oversized non-GIF candidates can be quarantined with their original bytes and index backed up.

These are notes about the project, not a claim that every provider or network failure has been eliminated.
